objectDesc.p: As per the description by Keith & Thomas (1935: 315, no. 5172), the text is written in Devanāgarī script across nine folios of paper, each measuring 6.5 by 3.5 inches.

handNote.p: Main hand of the manuscript, black ink, Devanagari script

normalization.p:
Our edition silently standardizes punctuation and normalizes spellings involving
the differences b/v; ...
-ṁ before independent vowel instead of -m plus dependent vowel
spelling errors involving confusion of the three sibilants
degemination of a consonant before v
editorial use of avagraha

app.note: Harunaga Isaacson points out to us that this verse is very similar to the opening verse of Anubhūti Svarūpācārya's Sārasvatavyākaraṇa: praṇamya paramātmānaṁ bāla-dhī-vr̥ddhi-siddhaye sārasvatīm r̥juṁ kurve prakriyāṁ nātivistarām
